title: Slide a rigid bar under a standoff bracket to its stop
instruction: Route the black bar under the grey bracket so it lies flat between the posts of both white clips, with its end within 8 mm of the red stop.
context: A rigid, pre-formed line has to pass beneath a standoff bracket, so it cannot be set down from above. Small-bore tubing, semi-rigid coax and bus bars are shaped before fitting and cannot be draped or pressed into place. Unlike pressing a cable into clips or dropping a part into an open fixture, the only way in is along the line's own axis under an overhang, so the part must be lowered beside the obstacle and slid. Here it travels through the 55 mm tunnel under the bracket's plate, then drops into two saddle clips, one either side of the bracket, with its end registered at a fitting (the stop) within 8 mm. The score pays for how far along that route the line got. A 1 g tabletop analogue of fitting lines on a spacecraft panel; no microgravity is claimed.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = +0.305. All objects are rigid and matte with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The channel line is x = 0.220, running along y. Fixed, grey (sRGB 0.6, 0.6, 0.6): the standoff bracket, a plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm (along x, along y, tall) centred at (0.220, 0.190) with its underside 55 mm above the table (centre height 60 mm), on two legs 10 x 60 x 55 mm centred at (0.175, 0.190) and (0.265, 0.190) (centre height 27.5 mm); the tunnel under the plate is 80 mm wide (x 0.180 to 0.260), 55 mm tall and open along y from y 0.160 to 0.220, and the legs close it from the sides. Fixed, white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.90), 12 mm tall (centre height 6 mm): clip A, two posts 10 x 15 mm centred at (0.202, 0.120) and (0.238, 0.120), their inner faces at x 0.207 and 0.233 (26 mm apart); clip B, the same pair at y = 0.230. Fixed, red (sRGB 0.8, 0.15, 0.1): the end stop, 30 x 5 x 12 mm centred at (0.220, 0.055) (centre height 6 mm), its face toward the bracket at y = 0.0575. Loose, black (sRGB 0.05, 0.05, 0.05): the bar, 16 x 16 mm square in section and 260 mm long, 42 g, lying on the table with its long axis along y, centred at (0.300, 0.360) (centre height 8 mm), so it spans y 0.230 to 0.490, parallel to the channel and 80 mm further from the arms. Nothing touches at the start; the bar's nearest neighbour is the far bracket leg, 24 mm away. Seated, the bar lies on the table along x = 0.220 from y 0.0615 to 0.3215, 4 mm short of the stop, with 5 mm of play per side in each clip; the plate covers the middle of that run, so the bar cannot be lowered into place from above. To build it: a 16 mm square aluminium tube with a 1 mm wall (about 42 g), painted or anodised black, or a printed bar of the same size and mass; the bracket, posts and stop printed or cut from wood and taped or glued directly to the table at the stated positions (or to a board no thicker than 1 mm that also lies under the bar's start position), with the channel line marked. Every height, including the 3 mm FLAT test, is measured from the surface the bar lies on.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released the bar and moved clear, from a top photo, a side photo and a tape measure. Four tests on the bar. FLAT: at rest (under 10 mm/s) with a face down (rolled less than 10 degrees from lying on one of its four long faces), its underside at both ends within 3 mm of the table top, so not propped on a post, a leg, the stop or the plate, and not balanced or leaning on an edge. THROUGH: over the whole 60 mm span of the plate (y 0.160 to 0.220) the bar's centreline lies inside the tunnel (x 0.180 to 0.260), so the bar passes under the plate. CLIPS: where it crosses y = 0.120 and y = 0.230 the centreline is within 6 mm of x = 0.220, which for a flat bar means between the posts of clip A and of clip B (5 mm of play, 1 mm allowed for the solver). END: the end face nearest the stop is 0 to 8 mm from the stop face; up to 2 mm of solver penetration counts as touching. Score: 1.0 FLAT, THROUGH, CLIPS and END; 0.75 FLAT, THROUGH and CLIPS with the end more than 8 mm from the stop; 0.5 FLAT and THROUGH but not between the posts of both clips (for example, short of clip A, or beside the posts); 0.25 either FLAT with the centreline inside the tunnel under at least 20 mm but not all 60 mm of the plate's span, or THROUGH and at rest but not FLAT with the underside at both ends at most 25 mm above the table (an end resting on a clip post or the stop, or the bar on an edge; 25 mm keeps the whole bar under the plate); 0 for everything else: beside the channel or the bracket, under less than 20 mm of the plate, partly under but not flat, on top of the plate, on an edge outside the tunnel, an end more than 25 mm up, standing on end, off the table, still moving or still held. Either end may lead and any of the four long faces may be down. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 state held for 1 s. In simulation every test uses the bar's centre and quaternion (its centreline and end points), not its axis-aligned bounds; FLAT uses resting(), the face-down test and the 3 mm test at both ends; the exact 8.0 mm gap, the exact 20 mm cover and the exact 25 mm height count (0.1 mm epsilon). The bracket, clips and stop are fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which any of them moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. In simulation release is inferred from the bar being at rest, so a bar held motionless in a scoring pose would also score; on real arms the score is read after the gripper has opened and moved clear.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the bar back on its marks, 80 mm beyond the channel line and parallel to it; the bracket, clips and stop do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: the line is a rigid 16 mm square tube, without the round section, bends or springiness of real tubing, coax or a bus bar; the clips are open saddles with 5 mm of play per side rather than snap-in P-clips; the stop only registers the end and nothing is screwed home. One shared friction pair, matte colours; the bracket, clips and stop are immovable. Earth gravity on a bench, which is also where this fit-up is done.
